title: Windshield Assembly Change to a Thicker Outer Ply with Revised Heater Terminal Arrangement
abstract: Windshield change to a thicker outer ply with the heater terminal moved out of the corner radius, in response to delamination at the terminal and to a premature outer ply crazing rate on the left-hand pane.

sections.reason: Delamination starting at the heater terminal in the lower forward corner was reported on fifty-eight windshields in four years, almost all of them on the left-hand pane, and the removal rate had reached one per eleven thousand flight hours against a target of one per thirty thousand. Twenty-two of the removals were for delamination alone and the rest for crazing of the outer ply, which was traced to the same local heat concentration. Two events produced an in-flight electrical smell and a diversion, so the change carries a safety justification as well as a reliability one.
sections.description: The windshield assembly is re-built with an outer ply 1.2 mm thicker and with the heater bus terminal moved 40 mm inboard of the corner radius so that the terminal heat no longer sits in the highest strain region of the pane. The bracket D5610112086631 is replaced to suit the new terminal position and the intercostal D5610119127963 is reworked locally to clear the relocated wiring. The doubler ARD967927-47 at the outboard reveal is retained and re-drilled. Tension bolts AES273284K7 and blind rivets AES757493-5D are renewed on removal. The heater feed harness is re-routed within the flight compartment in zones 211 and 213 and now runs behind the side console rather than over the reveal. Installation detail is on drawing D56101153469.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 4.9 kg per pane, 9.8 kg per aircraft, all of it forward of the flight compartment station with a longitudinal centre of gravity shift of 0.11 per cent mean aerodynamic chord that is declared and offset in the loading data. Heater electrical load is unchanged at the total but the peak current at switch-on falls by nine per cent. The pane is not interchangeable with the earlier assembly because the terminal position and the frame packing both change, and mixed left and right standards are permitted. The bird strike substantiation is re-run and the maximum demonstrated speed is unchanged.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN C00479 in April 2022. Retrofit is by Service Bulletin CRN-56-2004, normally at pane replacement rather than as a campaign, because the operator gets the benefit only when the pane is due anyway. One shift per pane with the aircraft on the ground.

type_data.balance_impact: Forward installation, longitudinal CG shift 0.11 % MAC, declared and reflected in the loading data
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00479, pane supply from a single source limited the ramp
